content.comment_body: I'm unable to download my Web Editor project to my [product_name] base module with article number [article_no]. When I attempt the download, I get an error stating: 'LWE project can only be downloaded into BM [article_no] or later version.' I looked on the website for a module ending in [article_no], but couldn't find anything. Can anyone assist?

The Web Editor project isn’t compatible with a [product_name] module ending in [article_no] in its article number. You can only load the Web Editor project onto the latest generation of [product_name] base modules, which have article numbers ending in [article_no] and are not currently offered for sale. I personally ordered a [product_name] with article number [article_no] directly from [company_name], but they haven't provided a delivery date yet.
I received confirmation on 20/12 for the new [product_name]. I placed my order on 11/12 and am looking forward to receiving it.
I received the new [product_name] today in the morning.

Hello, Just to clarify: The newest version of [product_name] that supports custom web pages created with [product_name] Web Editor will only run on [product_name] base modules with new order numbers: [article_no]. The key change is in the middle section of the article number, and the ending starts with [article_no]. Hope this is helpful.

However, when I upload my project from Web Editor, I receive the error: 'LWE project can only be uploaded from BM [article_no] or later version.'

It's not possible to upload such a project to your module—this function only works for the current [product_name] [version_no]. Refer to the article number in the post above. analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering compatibility problems when trying to deploy projects made with [product_name] Web Editor onto certain base modules. The reported error messages highlight mismatches between the project requirements and hardware versions. There’s confusion about the meaning of the article numbers and uncertainty regarding which modules support advanced Web Editor features. The lack of clear product and compatibility information is leading to user frustration and repeated questions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy process for deploying Web Editor projects to their [product_name] hardware, along with straightforward information about hardware and software compatibility. They also seek accessible details regarding which article numbers and module versions offer the desired features.
